summary: Deferred serialization locks creating intermittent batch accumulation and p99 latency bursts
description:
Issue summary: Intermittent p95/p99 latency bursts and request timeouts for NovaML on prod-us-east. Pattern correlates with short-stream workloads (avg tokens < 40) and high concurrency. Symptoms appear as a sudden build-up of queued requests in the continuous coalescer that resolves after ~6-18s, producing p99 spikes and occasional 504s for client requests.

Impact: Several customer endpoints saw p99 climb from ~400ms baseline to 8-12s during bursts, resulting in ~0.6% 504s across their traffic window and degraded UX for chat features. This is customer-facing and affecting QoS for a dedicated tenant.

First observed: 2026-03-09 22:40 UTC (customer report). Pattern has recurred every ~10 minutes during sustained peak traffic windows.

Initial hypothesis: a serialization/flush operation (KV cache snapshot or model state checkpoint) is taking a global lock that blocks coalescer flush paths, causing batch accumulation and delayed flushes. The blocking appears to be deferred (async snapshot) but holds a mutex long enough to interfere with flush-critical sections when many short requests are queued.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use dedicated tenant with short, frequent requests (avg 15-50 tokens) at ~200 qps per region.
2) Ensure KV cache warmup/snapshotting is enabled (default config).
3) Observe coalescer/continuous-batcher metrics (batch-size, flush-latency, queue-depth).
4) When snapshot runs, flush-latency jumps and queued requests accumulate for up to ~18s.
5) Repeat under 3+ concurrent model variants to increase lock contention.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 01:05 - Confirmed correlation between kv-snapshot duration and spikes in coalescer flush latency via trace spans (trace IDs in logs).

2026-03-10 03:12 - Reproduced locally with synthetic short-stream load against a staging cluster with snapshotting enabled; lock hold times matched prod pattern when multiple model variants snapshot overlapped.

2026-03-10 06:00 - Observed that snapshot code takes a per-model global serialization mutex that is held while writing snapshot chunks to storage; because flush-critical sections read the same in-memory structures, they block on the mutex path in the current implementation.

2026-03-11 09:20 - Hypothesis: Lock is safe for correctness but too coarse-grained. Under dedicated tenant multi-variant traffic, overlapping snapshots cause head-of-line blocking of batch flushers, producing request accumulation and p99 spikes.
2026-03-11 12:40 - Temporary mitigation tested: staggered snapshot schedule per-tenant and early-release of non-critical snapshot state reduced observed p99 by ~85% in a canary for NovaML.

2026-03-12 08:10 - Proposed long-term fixes: shard serialization mutex by KV segment, perform snapshot write without holding the flush-critical lock, or perform a copy-on-write delta and snapshot the delta asynchronously. A PR is in progress (see related_github_prs).
2026-03-12 12:50 - Load test with fix candidate (PR branch) shows stable p99 under the same synthetic workload; plan for small rollout to NovaML dedicated pool pending validation.

2026-03-10 03:25 - Marco Reyes (SRE): 'Initial triage: we see periodic long-running KV snapshots holding a serialization mutex that coincides with batcher flush delays. Working on mitigation.'

2026-03-11 13:05 - Aisha Kumar (Support): 'Applied staggered snapshot schedule to NovaML as a temporary mitigation at 12:30 UTC. Early metrics show p99 improved and 504s dropped to near-zero in the canary window.'
2026-03-12 09:15 - Marco Reyes (SRE): 'Rolling a fix candidate (PR 4123) to a small subset of dedicated pools for further validation. If stable, will schedule progressive rollout.'
resolution: Mitigation applied: snapshot schedule staggered for NovaML and snapshoter configured to early-release non-critical locks. Temporary mitigation reduced p99 spikes by ~85%. Root cause identified as coarse-grained serialization mutex in KV snapshot path contending with coalescer flush. Long-term fix in PR: shard locks and perform copy-on-write snapshotting to avoid blocking flush-critical paths. Rollout plan: canary -> progressive deployment across dedicated pools after 48h validation.
